description: Versioned evaluation workloads. A workload's version changes whenever its method changes; results are comparable only between runs of the same workload version. status 'implemented' means the workload is in the target image; 'defined' means its measurements are specified here and its implementation is scheduled for the stage named.

measurements.method: SHA-256 over a 64 KiB buffer on one thread for a fixed time (integer and bit operations)
the same on one thread per online CPU, summed (multi-core scaling)
96x96 double-precision matrix multiplication on one thread for a fixed time
random malloc and free of 16 B to 128 KiB blocks across 4096 slots, touching each block
map 64 MiB of anonymous memory with huge pages disabled, touch every page, unmap; repeated for a fixed time
fill a 64 MiB buffer; best round
copy a 64 MiB buffer; best round
a[i] = b[i] + s*c[i] over 64 MiB arrays of doubles, counting three arrays moved; best round
write a 256 MiB file to /data in 1 MiB blocks, timed through fsync
read the file back in 1 MiB blocks with O_DIRECT
random 4 KiB O_DIRECT reads for a fixed time
random 4 KiB O_DIRECT writes for a fixed time, timed through a final fdatasync
4 KiB append followed by fdatasync, repeated for a fixed time
read /dev/hwrng through the selected strategy: a 16-byte sample that identifies the provider, then throughput over half a second

a Wayland client draws a fixed animated scene with the CPU into shared-memory buffers and submits frames as fast as it can for a fixed time, full screen at the display resolution; frame rate, frame-time percentiles, and the rate at which frames reached the display

a fixed animated OpenGL ES 2.0 scene (a full-screen procedural shader and 64 blended quads), each frame finished before it is submitted, as fast as possible for a fixed time; frame rate, frame-time percentiles, displayed rate, and the renderer used
the same scene drawn with Vulkan, each frame finished before it is presented, as fast as possible for a fixed time; frame rate, frame-time percentiles, displayed rate, and the device used

a Flutter application animates a painted background with 64 shapes under a grid of 24 text widgets for a fixed time; Flutter draws one frame per display refresh, so the frame rate is bounded by the 60 Hz display; frame rate and percentiles of frame build and raster time

decode a fixed reference stream (1280x720, 25 frames/s, 5 s) as fast as possible with FFmpeg on all CPUs, once per case: each video codec (MPEG-2, AVC, HEVC) in each container (MP2TS, MP4, MSE-style fragments appended to the decoder's input); media seconds decoded per second, averaged over rounds until one second of decoding is timed
the same for 30 s audio streams, one per case: MP2 and AC-3 in MP2TS, AAC in MP4, HE-AAC in MP4 and in MP2TS

play a reference stream in real time, full screen, with its sound on the target's audio device, once per case (stream and graphics technology): frames the player did not show, as mpv counts them for Wayland, OpenGL ES and Vulkan output, and as the Flutter application counts them; by default one stream per video codec, each arriving a different way (MPEG-2 in MP2TS, AVC in MP4, HEVC as fragments)
frames dropped while WPE WebKit plays a fixed reference stream appended through MSE
fixed animated page rendered by WPE WebKit at 720p, 1080p and 4K
